name: Vladislawww/air-raid-alert-forecast (Air Raid Alert Forecast, Kyiv)
year: 2026 (repo created 2026-10-11, single commit 00e7e77 on 2026-10-12, the cohort deadline day)
authors: Vladislawww (commit author 'Vlad'); README states it was built in dialogue with Claude and Gemini
popularity: 0 GitHub stars at time of review (2026-10-17); no license file
peer_review_status: student repo; all numbers self-reported, not independently reproduced here (data not shipped)
target_type: onset (new start). The README explicitly documents switching away from a trivial 'is there an alert' state target to 'will a new alert start'.
target_definition: For each UTC hour t where Kyiv city is not under alert, y(t)=1 if at least one merged Kyiv-city alert interval starts in (t, t+1h]. H=1 (constant in main.py). Grid runs from the first Kyiv alert to floor(max finished_at) - H.
spatial_unit: city: Kyiv City (oblast value 'm. Kyiv' in official_data_uk.csv) only; other oblasts are used only as features
at_risk_masking: Yes. Hours where Kyiv is active at t (merged interval start <= t < finish) are dropped from training, validation and test ('eligible' rows). No explicit unit test asserts this; it is a single filter in pipeline.load_eligible().
data_sources: Vadimkin/ukrainian-air-raid-sirens-dataset, official_data_uk.csv (Ukrainian-name variant), 2022-03-15 to 2026-09-07; model trained only on data from 2024-01-01. An exploratory script (build_combined.py) tried to append JustJimer/ukraine-air-alert-stats archive/alerts_in_ua.csv after 2026-09-07, but the author did not use it for the final model.
data_source_variant: Official channel (Ukrainian-language file), not volunteer data. Admin levels: all rows sharing the 'oblast' column value are unioned via merge_intervals (so for other oblasts raion/hromada alerts are included in the union; for Kyiv City only city-level rows exist). Snapshot ends 2026-09-07 (frozen at the yellow/red reform). The unused alerts.in.ua stitch kept only alert_type == air_raid and excluded Crimea and Luhanska.
preprocessing: Per-region dedup on (started_at, finished_at) (not full-row dedup); Kyiv: 4141 records -> 2267 unique alerts (README says pre-2026 alerts were all doubled, found from even monthly counts). Overlapping intervals merged into a union per region. No gap handling: the 2026-08-30 to 09-01 recording gap falls inside the test window and its hours are treated as 'no alert' eligible negatives. No standing-alert handling for neighbour features (multi-month hromada alerts would keep e.g. Kharkivska act flag permanently 1). Luhanska is NOT excluded in the final pipeline (only in the unused stitching script). Calendar in Europe/Kyiv; everything else UTC.
known_label_artefacts: Duplicates: handled (dedup on start/finish pair per oblast; diagnose.py counts extra copies by year). Recording gap 30 Aug - 1 Sep 2026 (and partial 29 Aug / 2 Sep): NOT handled; hours counted as unmasked negatives inside the test, slightly depressing the test base rate and biasing Brier/PR-AUC. Standing alerts (439-604 day hromada alerts): NOT handled; affects neighbour 'act_o*' and 'n_active_oblasts' features rather than the Kyiv target. Exactly-30-minute ('naive') durations: not discussed; they enter kyiv_last_dur_h and the merged intervals unchanged. Luhanska permanent alert: kept as a near-constant feature. Swapped columns: not discussed. In build_combined.py open alerts older than 1 day at snapshot time were dropped as occupied-territory standing alerts and fresh open alerts closed at snapshot time (uses snapshot time, not causal), but that file was not used for the model.
model_family: Random Forest (sklearn, 300 trees, min_samples_leaf=30, max_features='sqrt') + Platt scaling (logistic regression on logit(p), C=1e6). Compared in walk-forward against logistic regression, LightGBM and HistGradientBoosting (compare_models.py). NOTE: the README 'How it works' section and final_eval.py print labels still say 'LightGBM', but pipeline.make_model() returns a RandomForestClassifier and the results table says 'Random Forest + Platt' - documentation inconsistency.
features: Kyiv own history: alert starts in last 1/3/6/24/72 h (windows (t-w, t]), hours since last merged alert ended (capped at 720 h), duration of the last finished alert. Spatial: for EVERY other oblast (about 25 incl. Kyivska and Luhanska), binary active-at-t flag and count of starts in the last hour (~50 columns, no border table); n_active_oblasts count. Calendar (Kyiv local): hour, day of week, hour_sin, hour_cos; 'month' built but dropped after walk-forward ablation (risk of memorising months). No external features (no ISW, Telegram, weather, launches).
external_feature_timing: Not applicable - no external features used. All features come from the alert log itself.
ablation_design: Yes, on the same sample: evaluate_folds.py and compare_models.py evaluate all variants (constant, hour, Kyiv-oblast-only, logistic regression, LightGBM with/without month, RF, HGB) on identical 6 walk-forward 2-month windows before the test, with identical training data starting 2024-01-01. Training-start choice (2022-03 / 2023-07 / 2024-01 / 2024-07) compared only with naive baselines on a 2-month validation window (baseline.py); the author admits differences were within noise.
split_scheme: Chronological by date. Test = last 2 months: from eligible.index.max() - 2 months, i.e. ~2026-07-07 to 2026-09-07 (1346 eligible hours, 143 onsets). Model selection: 6 consecutive 2-month walk-forward windows before the test (~2025-07 to 2026-07), each trained on 2024-01-01 up to the window start minus a 1-hour gap (expanding window). Final model: one fit on 2024-01-01 to test start minus 1 h; no refit inside test.
metrics: PR-AUC (average precision), lift = PR-AUC / base rate, Brier, log loss, mean predicted probability, top-k% capture and precision (top 5/10/20%), 5-bin quantile reliability table. No ROC-AUC, no Brier skill score reported explicitly.
unit_of_metric: Single unit (Kyiv City), so pooled = within-unit; not comparable to multi-oblast pooled AUCs.
baseline_strength: Weak-to-moderate baselines only: constant train mean (Brier 0.0971), hour-of-day train rate (0.0966), and 'Kyiv oblast active at t' conditional train rate (0.0938, a partial calibrated persistence of a neighbour). No rolling recent-rate baseline and no own-state calibrated persistence. Implied BSS of RF+Platt (0.0918): ~0.055 vs constant, ~0.050 vs hour, ~0.021 vs Kyiv-oblast-active (computed here from the README table). Because the constant uses the stale train rate (~6%) while the test rate is 10.6%, a rolling 14-day rate would likely be a much harder bar [estimate, not run]. [uncertain]
calibration: Platt scaling fitted on pooled out-of-fold predictions from the 6 walk-forward windows (fold models), then applied to a DIFFERENT final model trained on all pre-test data (calibrator/model mismatch). calibrate.py compared Platt vs isotonic by fitting on folds 1-4 and evaluating on folds 5-6; README says raw RF probabilities were ~25% too high on validation. Reliability shown only as a 5-quantile-bin table (no plot).
calibration_under_drift: Explicitly reported failure: the base rate rose from ~6% (train) to 10.6% (test), and the calibrated model under-predicts on test (e.g. top quintile predicted 13.5% vs 19.8% observed). Mean prediction printed for each model, which is effectively calibration-in-the-large, but no recalibration on recent data was done; the author recommends recalibrating on fresh data and frames output as a relative-risk indicator.
uncertainty_of_gain: None. No bootstrap, no DM test; README only notes 'few events (143 positives), all numbers approximate'.
regime_coverage: Training 2024-01 onward spans the Jan-2025 drone surge and the Dec-2025 raion reform (the latter barely matters for a Kyiv-City target, but affects neighbour union features). Test (Jul-Sep 2026) ends at the Sep-2026 yellow/red reform; the new regime is not evaluated. The 6% -> 10.6% base-rate shift within the official data is itself a regime shift the model did not adapt to.
leakage_handling: Causal features: active/start counts use searchsorted with start <= t; 'hours since end' only uses intervals with finish <= t. Truncation test (test_no_leakage.py, a script not a pytest test): 25 random hours since 2024, data truncated to started_at <= t and future finish times replaced by t+365d, features recomputed and compared -> 0 differences. No negative control (no deliberately leaky feature shown to be caught). Purge: 1-hour GAP between train end and each validation/test start, correct for H=1. Missed: (1) recording gap not masked; (2) Platt calibrator fitted on fold-model predictions applied to a different final model; (3) predict.py reports a probability even if t is during the training period (only warns); (4) data_end = max finished_at, a statistic over the whole file used to set the grid end (benign); (5) standing alerts in neighbour features are not causally capped, but that is noise, not leakage, since the truncation test maps open alerts to 'still active'.
test_window_hygiene: README claims test 'opened once, after all decisions were made'; selection used only the 6 pre-test walk-forward windows. Not pre-registered and no audit trail beyond a single squashed commit. The README's top line ('~1.8x better than random') contradicts its table (lift 2.33), suggesting the test was run more than once across versions or the text was not updated [uncertain]. [uncertain]
headline_results: Test (2026-07-07 to 09-07, 1346 eligible hours, 143 onsets, base rate 10.6%): RF + Platt PR-AUC 0.247 (lift 2.33), Brier 0.0918; constant 0.106 / 1.00 / 0.0971; hour of day 0.131 / 1.24 / 0.0966; 'Kyiv oblast active' 0.146 / 1.37 / 0.0938. Top 10% riskiest hours capture 26.6% of onsets, top 20% capture 38.5%; top-5% precision 36.8% (3.5x base). Beats all included naive baselines on ranking and Brier, but the Brier gain is small (BSS ~0.02 vs the best baseline) and no rolling recent-rate baseline was tried. Walk-forward validation suggested ~3x lift; test is lower. Probabilities are under-calibrated on test due to the base-rate shift. README is internally inconsistent: headline sentence says ~1.8x, table says 2.33x.
code_available: Yes: ~870 lines of Python in a flat layout (main, features, pipeline, final_eval, predict, research scripts) plus a committed model artifact (artifacts/model.joblib). Data not included; user downloads official_data_uk.csv manually. requirements.txt is unpinned (pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, lightgbm, joblib), no Python version, no license, no tests framework (leakage check is a script). Single commit; comments and outputs in Ukrainian. Not maintained after the deadline.
takeaways_for_project: 1) Strong evidence for our D-021 rule that the ROLLING recent-rate baseline is the main bar: their frozen constant baseline used the ~6% train rate against a 10.6% test rate, so 'beating the constant' overstates skill; we must report BSS vs rolling recent rate. 2) Same failure mode we expect in the D-015 new-regime check: a frozen Platt calibrator under-predicts when the base rate shifts; our calibration-in-the-large row (mean predicted vs observed) per group is the right diagnostic, and we should show it on the official test too. 3) Fit any calibrator on validation predictions of the SAME frozen model (D-021), not on OOF predictions of different fold models. 4) Mask the 30 Aug - 1 Sep recording gap (D-013): their test silently includes it as negatives. 5) Neighbour features without the D-020 24h standing cap become constant flags (Kharkivska/Luhanska); keep the cap and exclude Luhanska. 6) Use a border table (D-017) rather than ~50 per-oblast columns, which overfit on a single target unit. 7) Their truncation test is a good template but lacks the negative control our tests/test_leakage.py requires. 8) Their 1h purge gap matches our purge rule for H=1. 9) Peer comparison caution: their metrics are for one city, so PR-AUC/lift are not comparable with our pooled 24-unit numbers; compare with our Kyiv City row only. 10) Top-k capture tables are an intuitive add-on for the README/app (M5).
best_practices: Adopt: onset target with at-risk masking; dedup before counting (they rediscovered the duplicate issue); identical walk-forward windows for all model/feature ablations; dropping features that can memorise time (month); truncation-based leakage check; honest Limitations section reporting under-calibration and validation-vs-test optimism; lift = PR-AUC / base rate as an interpretable secondary metric; top-k% capture tables. Avoid: stale train-mean constant as the only no-skill reference; calibrator fitted on a different model than the one deployed; no CI on the gain with only 143 positives; documentation drift (LightGBM vs RF, 1.8x vs 2.33x); unpinned requirements; leakage check as an ad-hoc script instead of a CI test; ignoring the recording gap; un-capped standing alerts in spatial features; choosing the training start by reasoning when validation differences are within noise without saying so up front (they did say so - good).
